pillar_reactions.evidence: The only pillar reached before the recording cuts off, and she engaged with it before it was even presented. She had already concluded from Trevor's videos that 'movement is extremely important, not only weight, but also like stretching and movement, which also nobody teaches you when you're younger.' She then volunteered exactly what she needs from coaching — technique breakdown — describing repeatedly pausing videos and still being unable to tell two similar movements apart: 'finally, when he broke it down, it really does help... I'm pretty technical, so you have to show me. Once you show me, I get it.'

The recording ends during the training and mobility pillar, before nutrition was reached. Worth flagging for whoever recovers the rest of the call: she follows a strict carnivore diet, has already lost 32 lb on it, weighs nothing, rejects the hormonal explanation for midlife weight gain outright, and had a bad prior experience with dietitians. The standard intermittent-fasting and whole-foods pitch would be landing on someone with strong, specific and already-successful nutritional convictions.

Not reached before the recording ends. Her own framing suggests it is the weakest fit of the three for her — 'I'm pretty easy going. So for me, as far as I get some kind of instructions to follow, I will follow' — and she already has an informal accountability partner in her son, whom she describes as a trainer who pushes her: 'it's never three or four. It's always up to eight.'

anchors.raw: when I was younger, I tried dietitians. That did not work. And I followed what they wrote religiously, to the point that I was weighing my food, which is kind of crazy, didn't help.
anchors.note: She has paid professionals for this problem before, complied fully, and got nothing. That is a specific and unaddressed objection to paying a professional again, and it was never surfaced or answered in the captured portion.

anchors.raw: I lost 32 pounds, so I think that's pretty successful just through diet and exercise, not popping any pills, not taking any shots, not doing any ozempics or any other crap that I refused to.
anchors.note: The strongest latent objection on the call. She has already achieved a substantial result alone and is proud of having done it without help or drugs, which makes the case for paying $6,000 harder rather than easier. The rep affirmed the achievement warmly and never converted it into a reason to buy.

anchors.raw: not popping any pills, not taking any shots, not doing any ozempics
anchors.note: She has explicitly ruled out the cheapest and fastest competing solution on ideological grounds, which removes the substitute that would otherwise dominate this demographic. Combined with her refusal of surgery and of conventional medicine generally, coaching is one of the few remaining routes she will accept.

anchors.raw: it's hard to tell women, you have to take care of yourself, you have to be healthy, you have to do this, that, if you don't represent it yourself
anchors.note: She runs a wellness practice and is planning retreats, so her own physique is a professional asset. The rep picked this up and told a story about a mid-fifties yoga practitioner whose business benefited. It is the most commercially relevant lever on the call and it arrived organically.

anchors.raw: I feel I constantly have to be very strict regime to look the way I want to look. And I'm like, is there an easier way?... right now it feels like a, almost a full-time job.
anchors.note: She stated the value proposition herself: buy back the time and effort that maintaining her result currently costs. Nothing in the captured portion picked this up, and it is the single sentence a close should have been built on.

unmet_demand.want: A method that works on a 50-year-old female body rather than the one she trained in her twenties
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She framed this as her central hypothesis — 'maybe the problem is that I'm trying to train my body the way it used to train when I was younger. But the body changes and now it doesn't really react.' Nothing in the captured portion addresses female-specific or perimenopausal programming, and the rep's answer to her being a woman was that Trevor works with a fair share of women across all ages. She had also just rejected the hormonal explanation outright, which nobody engaged with either way.

unmet_demand.want: Movement she can perform safely with a cervical disc problem, damaged knees and an inherited spinal predisposition
unmet_demand.why_unmet: She is already doing halos and around-the-worlds, which take a loaded bell around the head and neck, self-taught from video. No screening question was asked, no clearance was suggested and no contraindication was named. What she received was an assurance that knee and shoulder problems resolve within two to three months.

unmet_demand.want: A way to hold her result without a permanently strict regime
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The most clearly articulated need on the call and the one the offer is arguably built for. The recording ends before the nutrition pillar, which is where sustainability would have been addressed, so it is unresolved rather than unserved.

unmet_demand.want: To fold the training into the wellness retreats she is planning to run
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep raised it himself — 'maybe you incorporate this into some of your retreats' — without any position on whether the programme permits teaching its methods commercially. She is a practitioner buying partly for professional reasons and there is no stated policy on that at all.
